claims.text: Every released DIRD carries the line: 'Comments or questions pertaining to this document should be addressed to [name redacted under (b)(3) 10 USC 424 and (b)(6)], AAWSA Program Manager, Defense Intelligence Agency, ATTN: [redacted], Bldg 6000, Washington, DC 20340-5100.' The AAWSAP program manager post is therefore documented in primary record; the incumbent's name is withheld in the DIA release.

DIA Info Memo U-429-09 refers to 'The program manager, [redacted], has reviewed all of the papers and concurs with the reviews' — establishing a single named DIA officer who personally reviewed every FY2009 DIRD.

Identification of the redacted AAWSA Program Manager as Dr. James T. Lacatski is not established by any primary document reached in this pass. It rests on his own published accounts and on secondary reporting. Treat the name as unconfirmed against the FOIA record until a document with the name unredacted (or a DIA org chart / personnel record) is located.

label: James T. Lacatski
narrative: Lacatski is the single most load-bearing name in the funded lineage: he is the DIA official who conceived, wrote and ran the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program. He is named in the open record as 'Government Project Leader, Dr. James T. Lacatski' on the August 2008 DIA solicitation HHM402-08-R-0211, which is the only place in the entire AAWSAP paper trail where the program manager is not redacted — DIA scrubbed his name from every later FOIA release under 10 USC 424 but missed it in the original public bid notice. A rocket scientist by training (D.Eng.), Lacatski approached Robert Bigelow in 2007 after reading Kelleher and Knapp's 'Hunt for the Skinwalker', and by his own account the June 19, 2007 letter he sent Bigelow on DIA letterhead is what set the whole thing in motion — DIA later told The Black Vault (FOIA-00023-2022) it could locate no such letter, a records outcome the board treats as an artifact rather than a refutation. He directed the 38 Defense Intelligence Reference Documents, personally reviewed all of them, and per DIA's own 30 October 2009 memo concurred with the outside reviewers' assessments. He is the co-author, with Colm Kelleher and George Knapp, of 'Skinwalkers at the Pentagon' (2021) and of the 'Inside the U.S. Government Covert UFO Program' series (2023, 2025, and 'Future Visions'), all cleared through DOPSR — meaning DoD read and passed the manuscripts. Lacatski has stated that he personally entered a craft of unknown origin, and in an April 2026 conversation with Jeremy Corbell he said AAWSAP 'created the world's largest UFO data warehouse' of more than 100 detailed reports, that he doubts the files will ever be released, and hinted that a smaller focused effort connected to the proposed KONA BLUE successor continued after AAWSAP ended.
